mainTopic: The wording of הבדלה: עולא's one-line הבדלה, the story of how it was reported, and a ברייתא about which ברכות open and close with 'ברוך', brought to challenge it.
overview: This amud opens by ending the previous discussion: the הלכה does not follow the opinion just quoted, and instead follows שמואל. The גמרא then tells a story. רב יהודה sends his son רב יצחק to bring the visiting sage עולא a basket of fruit and watch how he makes הבדלה. רב יצחק sends אביי instead. אביי reports that עולא said only 'ברוך המבדיל בין קודש לחול' and nothing more. רב יהודה scolds his son, because his pride means the teaching will be credited to אביי and not to him. The גמרא then challenges עולא's short form from a ברייתא. The ברייתא teaches that every ברכה opens and closes with 'ברוך', except for a list of exceptions: some open without closing, some close without opening, and הטוב והמטיב is a special case. The גמרא draws out the challenge against עולא and deals with it on the next amud.

steps.title: The הלכה does not follow the previous opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the opinion just cited is not the הלכה. The הלכה follows שמואל instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is not like him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the previous discussion about how to word הבדלה by ruling against the opinion it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this line, the גמרא presented different views on how the הבדלה blessing should be phrased. This short line decides the matter: the view just stated is rejected, and the practical הלכה follows שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Like him, in accordance with his view

phrases.english: And the halacha is not in accordance with him.
phrases.notes: This turns down the view just mentioned about how to word הבדלה. The הלכה follows שמואל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion from the previous amud.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The opinion just cited about הבדלה wording is not the practical הלכה. The הלכה follows שמואל.

steps.title: רב יהודה sends his son to observe עולא's הבדלה
steps.stepSummary: עולא visits פומבדיתא. רב יהודה tells his son רב יצחק to bring עולא a gift of fruit and watch how he makes הבדלה. רב יצחק sends אביי in his place.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא came to פומבדיתא. רב יהודה said to his son רב יצחק: Go bring him a basket of fruit, and see how he makes הבדלה. He did not go; he sent אביי to him instead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that will show us how the great sage עולא actually said הבדלה. This step sets up the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה wants to learn the correct הבדלה text from a live example, so he sends his son with a gift as a polite way to visit. The key twist is that רב יצחק does not go himself and sends the young אביי instead. That choice sets up the scolding later in the story.

phrases.english: Ulla happened to come to Pumbedita,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה לְרַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said to Rav Yitzchak his son:
Go bring him a basket of fruit,
and see how he makes havdala.
phrases.notes: This is the real purpose of the visit.

phrases.english: He did not go; he sent Abaye to him.
phrases.notes: אביי was a young student at the time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from ruling about הבדלה wording to a story showing what one sage actually said.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup only: the story will report עולא's actual הבדלה wording.

steps.title: אביי reports עולא's short הבדלה
steps.stepSummary: אביי comes back and reports that עולא said only 'ברוך המבדיל בין קודש לחול' and nothing more.
steps.simpleTranslation: When אביי came back, רב יצחק said to him: How did he say it? He said to him: He said 'Blessed is He Who distinguishes between holy and profane,' and nothing more.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tells רב יצחק exactly what עולא said for הבדלה. It was one short line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The important detail is 'ותו לא', meaning 'and nothing more'. עולא did not list the other הבדלות and did not add a separate closing ברכה. He said just one short sentence that starts with 'ברוך'.

keyTerms.meaning: Who distinguishes between holy and profane

steps.whatToRemember: עולא's הבדלה was only one sentence: 'ברוך המבדיל בין קודש לחול', with nothing added.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא אַבָּיֵי, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הֵיכִי אָמַר?
phrases.english: When Abaye came, he said to him: How did he say it?
phrases.notes: רב יצחק is the one asking.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: ״בָּרוּךְ הַמַּבְדִּיל בֵּין קוֹדֶשׁ לְחוֹל״
phrases.english: He said to him: 'Blessed is He Who distinguishes between holy and profane'
he said, and nothing more.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא אַבָּיֵי, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הֵיכִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports the result of the errand set up in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How did עולא word his הבדלה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He said only 'ברוך המבדיל בין קודש לחול', with nothing more.

steps.title: רב יצחק tells his father what אביי reported
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה asks his son how עולא made הבדלה. רב יצחק admits he did not go, and repeats אביי's report.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before his father. He said to him: How did he say it? He said to him: I did not go; I sent אביי, and he told me: 'Who distinguishes between holy and profane.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק returns to his father with the answer, but he admits he got it secondhand from אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The content of the report is the same as before. What is new is that רב יהודה now learns his son did not go himself. That admission sets up the rebuke in the next step.

phrases.english: He came before his father,
he said to him: How did he say it?
phrases.notes: Now רב יהודה is the one asking.

phrases.english: He said to him: I did not go,
I sent Abaye,
and he told me: 'Who distinguishes between holy and profane.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Passes the report from step 3 up to רב יהודה, and reveals the son did not go himself.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רב יהודה asks how עולא made הבדלה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'המבדיל בין קודש לחול', learned through אביי.

steps.title: רב יהודה rebukes his son's pride
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה tells his son that his pride caused him to lose the chance to have this teaching reported in his own name.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Your greatness and your pride, master, caused you that you will not say the teaching from his mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה scolds רב יצחק for sending someone else instead of going himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because רב יצחק felt too important to carry the fruit basket, he did not hear עולא directly. As a result, the teaching will be passed down through אביי and not credited to רב יצחק. The lesson is that humility brings you closer to Torah firsthand.

keyTerms.meaning: The teaching from his mouth, firsthand

steps.whyThisMatters: This story shows the value of learning directly from a teacher. It also explains why this הבדלה report comes to us through אביי.

phrases.english: He said to him: The master's haughtiness,
phrases.notes: 'מר' (master) is a polite, here ironic, way of addressing his son.

phrases.english: and the master's pride,
caused the master
that you will not report the teaching from his own mouth.
phrases.notes: Meaning: the teaching will not be credited to you, but to אביי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the son's admission in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pride caused רב יצחק to miss hearing the teaching firsthand, so it will not be said in his name.

steps.title: A ברייתא: every ברכה opens and closes with ברוך
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to challenge עולא's short הבדלה from a ברייתא. The ברייתא says every ברכה opens and closes with 'ברוך', except for a few listed types.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: All blessings open with 'ברוך' and close with 'ברוך', except for blessings over מצוות, blessings over fruit, a blessing that follows right after another blessing, and the last blessing of שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge עולא's practice. This step starts the attack, and the ברייתא continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sets a general rule: a ברכה needs 'ברוך' at both its opening and its closing. Only a few types are exempt. הבדלה is not on this exception list. So it seems it should be a longer ברכה with its own closing 'ברוך', not one short line like עולא said.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection, from a תנאי source
A blessing that comes right after another blessing

steps.confusionAlert: The quote is not finished here. The ברייתא continues in steps 7 and 8. The גמרא spells out how this ברייתא challenges עולא, and deals with that challenge, on the next amud.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
All the blessings, all of them,
one opens with 'Baruch' and closes them with 'Baruch',
except for blessings over מצוות and blessings over fruit,
phrases.notes: These are short ברכות with only one 'ברוך'.

phrases.english: and a blessing juxtaposed to another blessing,
phrases.notes: For example, the middle ברכות of the שמונה עשרה, which rely on the 'ברוך' of the ברכה before them.

phrases.english: and the last blessing of Shema,

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: כׇּל הַבְּרָכוֹת כּוּלָּן פּוֹתֵחַ בְּבָרוּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses a ברייתא to attack the short הבדלה wording that עולא used in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's one-line הבדלה, 'ברוך המבדיל בין קודש לחול', with nothing more.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires every ברכה, apart from listed exceptions, to open and close with 'ברוך'. הבדלה is not listed as an exception, so it should have a full opening and a closing ברכה.

steps.title: The two kinds of exceptions to the rule
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains its exceptions. Some ברכות open with ברוך but do not close with it. Others close with ברוך but do not open with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: For some of them open with 'ברוך' and do not close with 'ברוך', and some of them close with 'ברוך' and do not open with 'ברוך'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the ברייתא from step 6. Here the ברייתא explains why the listed ברכות are exceptions to the rule that every ברכה opens and closes with ברוך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Short ברכות, like ברכת המצות and ברכת הפירות, open with ברוך but have no closing line. A ברכה הסמוכה לחברתה, meaning a ברכה that comes right after another ברכה, closes with ברוך but does not open with it, because the ברוך of the ברכה before it counts as its opening. So the exceptions only remove the opening or the closing in specific cases. The basic rule of opening and closing still stands for everything else.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברכה said before doing a מצוה; short, so it has only an opening
A ברכה that comes right after another ברכה; it has only a closing

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think these ברכות are not real ברכות. They are full ברכות. They only skip the opening ברוך or the closing ברוך because of how they are built.

phrases.english: For some of them open with 'Blessed'
phrases.notes: For example, blessings over מצוות and over food.

phrases.english: and do not close with 'Blessed',
and some of them close with 'Blessed'
phrases.notes: For example, a blessing that follows right after another blessing.

phrases.english: and do not open with 'Blessed'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 6 by explaining how each listed exception differs from the main rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Some ברכות have only an opening ברוך, and some have only a closing ברוך.

steps.title: הטוב והמטיב is an unusual case
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that הטוב והמטיב opens with ברוך and does not close with ברוך.
steps.simpleTranslation: And 'הטוב והמטיב' opens with 'ברוך' and does not close with 'ברוך'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by pointing out one surprising ברכה, הטוב והמטיב. This completes the source the גמרא uses to challenge עולא, and the challenge is spelled out on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הטוב והמטיב is the fourth ברכה of ברכת המזון. It comes right after another ברכה, so by the rule in step 7 we would expect it to close with ברוך and not open with it. Instead it does the opposite: it opens with ברוך and has no closing. The ברייתא lists it on its own because it does not fit the usual pattern.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He Who is good and does good', the fourth ברכה of ברכת המזון

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's main rule is that every ברכה opens and closes with ברוך. The only exceptions are the specific ones it lists. הבדלה is not on that list, so it should open and close with ברוך. עולא's one-line הבדלה did not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the source text. On the next amud the גמרא uses it to challenge עולא: a full הבדלה should seem to need a closing ברוך, which his one-line version lacked.

phrases.english: And 'He Who is good and does good' opens with 'Blessed'
phrases.notes: Even though it follows another blessing in ברכת המזון.

phrases.english: and does not close with 'Blessed'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds one more special case to the exceptions explained in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הטוב והמטיב opens with ברוך and does not close with ברוך.
